text: Eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong. How can I blaspheme my king, who has saved me?
I am the wheat of God, and let me be ground by the teeth of the wild beasts, that I may be found the pure bread of Christ.
Where the bishop is present, there let the multitude be, just as where Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic Church.
The glory of God is a living man, and the life of man consists in beholding God.
He became what we are, that he might make us what he is.
The blood of the martyrs is the seed of the Church.
What has Athens to do with Jerusalem? What concord is there between the Academy and the Church?
He cannot have God for his Father who has not the Church for his Mother.
source: On the Unity of the Catholic Church 6

text: He was made man that we might be made God.
Unless he were divine, none would be saved; unless he were truly human, none would be raised.
A tree is known by its fruit; a man by his deeds. A good deed is never lost.
What has not been assumed has not been healed; it is what is united to his divinity that is saved.
Concepts create idols; only wonder grasps anything.
If you cannot find Christ in the beggar at the church door, you will not find him in the chalice.
Glory to God for all things.
You have made us for yourself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.
Late have I loved you, beauty so old and so new; late have I loved you.
Love, and do what you will.
source: Homilies on the First Epistle of John 7.8

text: Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.
When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
Christian, recognize your dignity, and becoming a partner in the divine nature, refuse to return to the old baseness by degenerate conduct.
Listen, my son, to the master's instructions, and incline the ear of your heart.
Ora et labora — pray and work.
Theology without action is the theology of demons.
I do not worship matter; I worship the God of matter, who became matter for my sake.
I no longer fear God; I love him. For love casts out fear.
If sinners would only weep for what they have done, they would teach the angels how to praise.
Whatever has been said well by anyone belongs to us Christians.
If you do not hope, you will not find what is beyond your hopes.
Scripture grows with its readers.
